Quotation < R30,000 Procurement Method

Simple procurement method for procuring goods or services with estimated value below R30,000.

Process:

  1. Demand Identification - End-user identifies need
  2. Requisition Capture - SCM system entry
  3. Obtain Written Quotation(s) - Minimum 1 quotation
  4. Evaluation & Selection - Price reasonableness check
  5. Approval of Award - Delegated authority approval
  6. Purchase Order Issued - PO generation
  7. Delivery/Service - End-user confirmation
  8. Invoice & Payment - Standard payment processing
PPPFA regulations; National Treasury SCM Instruction Notes; PFMA Section 76; Constitution Section 217
Simplest procurement method for low-value procurements. No formal advertisement required. Single quotation acceptable.

Open Request for Quotation - R30,000 to R300,000

Open competitive procurement method for goods and services in the R30,000 to R300,000 range (Municipalities: R30,000-R300,000; Departments: R30,000-R1,000,000).
PPPFA; National Treasury SCM Instruction Notes; MFMA Section 111; PFMA Section 76; Constitution Section 217
Open competitive process. Minimum 3 quotations preferred. Must be advertised on portal and website.

Competitive Bid < R50 Million

Formal competitive bidding process for procurements between RFQ threshold and R50 million.
PPPFA; National Treasury SCM Instruction Notes; PFMA Section 76; MFMA Section 111; Constitution Section 217
Formal competitive bidding with BSC, BEC, and BAC processes. Preference points apply. Compliance verification required.

Competitive Bid > R50 Million

High-value competitive bidding process with extended timeline and formal oversight.
PPPFA; National Treasury SCM Instruction Notes; PFMA Section 76; MFMA Section 111; Constitution Section 217
High-value strategic procurement. Treasury concurrence required. Dedicated contract management.

Sole Source Procurement

Limited competition procurement for situations where only one supplier can provide the requirement.
PFMA Section 76; MFMA Section 111; Requires deviation approval
Non-competitive method requiring Accounting Officer approval. Price reasonableness verification essential.

Emergency/Deviation Procurement

Expedited procurement for unforeseen circumstances where competitive bidding is impractical.
PFMA Section 76; MFMA Section 111; Emergency provisions
Used only for genuine emergencies. Requires written motivation and Accounting Officer approval.

Panel Suppliers / Framework Agreement

Call-off procurement from pre-approved supplier panel or framework agreement.
PPPFA; Framework Agreement regulations; PFMA Section 76; MFMA Section 111
Used for repeat procurement from established supplier panels. Panel must have been established through competitive bidding.

80/20 Preference Point System

Price weighted at 80% and preference points weighted at 20%. Applicable to lower-value tenders (typically R30,000 - R500,000).
PPPFA Section 2; National Treasury Instruction Note on Procurement; B-BBEE Act

Applicable Range: R30,000 - R500,000

Preference Points: B-BBEE Contribution (20 points)

All 20 preference points allocated to B-BBEE contribution per PPPFA regulations.

90/10 Preference Point System

Price weighted at 90% and preference points weighted at 10%. Applicable to higher-value tenders (typically above R500,000).
PPPFA Section 2; National Treasury Instruction Note on Procurement; B-BBEE Act

Applicable Range: Above R500,000

Preference Points: B-BBEE Contribution (10 points)

All 10 preference points allocated to B-BBEE contribution per PPPFA regulations.
